title: SDK Rapid Onramp: Campfire Quicklab Notes
content:
Purpose: capture a lightweight, repeatable one-hour 'campfire' quicklab for new internal and pilot external devs that demonstrates a minimal end-to-end SDK integration, common failure modes, and easy wins for performance.

Context and constraints:
- Audience: backend engineers or product devs with basic HTTP experience (not LLM experts).
- Timebox: 60 minutes (40m guided coding + 20m troubleshooting + wrap).
- Environment: assume laptop (mac/linux), intermittent network, ability to run a small local test harness.
- Goal metrics: successful end-to-end call, streaming demo, telemetry emitted (latency, token usage), and one optimization applied (batching or cache).

Campfire format (timeline):
1) 0-5m: Welcome + 3-slide intent
   - Problem statement: shipping an LLM feature -> unpredictability in latency/cost/quality
   - Redwood value props to highlight: single API, predictable perf, local dev parity
2) 5-15m: Quick setup (pre-baked repo clone)
   - env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY (use test token), LOCAL_PROXY=false (note: offline shortcut)
   - commands: node/py minimal examples to install and run a smoke call
3) 15-40m: Guided lab tasks (incremental checkpoints)
   - Checkpoint A: make a simple text-generation call and print streaming tokens
   - Checkpoint B: add a function/tool call stub and validate structured output parsing
   - Checkpoint C: enable prefix caching (config toggle) and compare latency of repeated calls
4) 40-55m: Fault injection + recovery patterns
   - Simulate 5xx and network timeouts via a local proxy; exercise client retry/backoff and circuit-breaker settings
   - Show graceful fallback: route to smaller model variant or canned response
5) 55-60m: Wrap, ask for feedback, next steps

Developer notes + scripts to include in repo (short snippets in doc):
- Minimal smoke script: curl POST /v1/generate with small prompt, stream=true, print token deltas
- Local proxy: tiny script to delay responses and return configurable 5xx for N requests
- Telemetry shim: emit one-line JSON to stdout for latency, tokens_in, tokens_out, model

Checklist for facilitator before running:
- ✅ Ensure test API keys provisioned and rotated weekly for public pilots
- ✅ Repo seed has Dockerfile-free quickstart and a one-file example per language (py/js)
- ✅ Smoke harness includes deterministic prompt seeds for eval comparisons

Telemetry & gating (why this matters):
- Capture: initial call latency, streaming start time, total tokens, error counts, model variant used
- Use cases: early-warning if streaming start time > 200ms, or tokens blow past expected budget
- Quick alert rule: if error_rate > 5% during the campfire, switch to canned demo and log incident PR

Common gotchas & facilitator tips:
- Network flakiness will derail novices: show the local proxy first so they can experience both success and failure without external outages
- Token estimate mismatch: show how to calculate rough token counts for a prompt and how to use the model catalog to pick cheaper variants for prototyping
- CORS for web demos: prefer server-side examples or explain a simple proxy pattern

Open questions / follow-ups (action items):
- [DX-318] Create a 15-minute 'micro-version' for sales demos (Priya to prototype)
- Add a small i18n prompt example (Samir) to show token variance across languages
- Ship a guided notebook variant for local-mode (Marisol to carve time Q2 sprint)

Notes to self (stream-of-consciousness):
- Keep the lab repo < 10 files; cognitive load matters.
- Consider adding a 'failure-first' path where we intentionally break things early so learners build muscle memory on recovery.
- Potentially integrate a lightweight k6 script to demonstrate load and batching impact in 5 minutes.

Changelog (mini):
- 2025-02-05 initial draft
- 2025-02-20 added telemetry gating rules and facilitator checklist
- 2025-03-05 collaborator edits: added failure-first suggestion and micro-version action item

Quick link map for the repo to include in README:
- /examples/python/one_liner.py -> minimal generate + streaming example
- /tools/proxy/delay_proxy.py -> failure injection harness
- /docs/facilitator.md -> step-by-step facilitator script + troubleshooting FAQ

End of notes. This is intentionally conversational; convert to README + facilitator guide when we stabilize the flow.
